description: Discovery by DNS and handles (spec/SPEC.md §12, L2; added 2026-10-26). "presentation" holds TXT records written as text (§12.2 item 7) and their character-strings, as strings_hex, or resolve-failed. "txt" holds the TXT records a lookup of txt_name gave (null: none is asked), each a list of strings, and where they lead: the key the record must agree with (null without a bag record), the org's address record URL and its origin, or resolve-failed (§12.2 items 1 to 4). "agreement" holds the key a TXT names, an org record, the record a reader had pinned, the verdict of the record's agreement with the TXT (§12.2 item 5) and the key pinned after the reading (§7.3). "handles" holds strings read as handles (§12.3 item 1), with their local part, domain and record path, or bad-address. "cases" holds signed handle records with their canonical strings, digests and signers, and their verdict for a reader that expects an org key and a handle and holds the org's revoked list, at several times (§12.4 item 3). "invalid" holds handle records that break their form, and "parse" bytes read as a handle record.
suite_parameters: Ed25519 signatures; sealing with RFC 9180 base mode, DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) (kem 0x0020), HKDF-SHA256 (kdf 0x0001), AES-256-GCM (aead 0x0002)
test_data: Every seed, private key, content key and nonce in this file is test data, fixed by construction: seeds are one byte repeated 32 times, and the rest comes from a seeded xorshift128+. They are public; never let them protect anything real.
notes: A TXT record is a bag record when its first field is v=ac1; a reader joins its strings with nothing between them, ignores spaces and tabs around fields and empty fields, ignores unknown fields and refuses one given twice; key is required, host is exactly bag or absent, and a rec field is refused: DNS names no URL. Two bag records, or a malformed one, are resolve-failed with no fallback to the well-known URL. The origin is https://bag.<domain> with host=bag, else https://<domain>; no TXT is asked for a name over 253 characters or under a special-use name.

A record agrees with its TXT when its key is the TXT key, or when its rotated_from is the TXT key and its rotation_sig verifies under it (one countersigned step); anything else is resolve-failed before any pin is read. The pin then moves only by §7.3: DNS never moves a pin.

A handle record is checked in this order: its form, its signature under its org, iat <= now + skew, now <= iat + ttl, its org and handle against the expected ones (resolve-failed), its address against the revoked list (revoked). Relays store no handle record. A handle finds an address and admits no one.
